metadata.name: CORE — Output language
metadata.usage: Load on every request that generates text, code comments meant for people, interface copy, or documents. The library itself stays in English.

deteccion.regla: Detect the language of the user's current request from the words they wrote.
Generate new documents, interface copy, user-visible messages, domain names in examples, and narrative report text in that language.
If the user explicitly requests a language, use that language for every generated text, even when the request is written in another language.
If the request mixes languages and does not name one, use the language of the instruction, not of a pasted source document.

proyecto_existente.regla: When editing an existing file, keep that file's language unless the user asked for a language or asked to translate it.
New strings added to an existing interface follow the language already used by that interface, unless the user requested another language.

que_no_se_traduce.regla: Do not translate file paths, XML tags, phase ids, mode ids (validar, continuo), status tokens, protocol keywords, or identifiers required by a contract.
Conventional Commit types stay the specification keywords. The summary follows the selected language.
Literal messages required by an approved story stay exact, in the language of that story.

codigo.regla: Comments, UI strings, validation messages, and documentation created for the product follow the selected language.
Programming-language keywords, library names, and existing symbols stay as they are.
